title: Vocabulary: natural, flexible language for Speaking
status: Owner approved v1.0.0 on 2026-10-26; teacher release to all eligible schools (optional vocabulary lesson)
rights: Original Brains Heist LLC instructional material, AI-assisted. Passages, people and data are fictional and created for practice. Not official IELTS material. Human editorial and classroom review recommended.
prerequisites: Lesson 4 (Speaking Part 1) and Lesson 12 (Speaking Part 2 long turn).
Learners have given at least one Part 2 talk.
Optional vocabulary lesson: use when spoken answers repeat 'good', 'nice' and 'very' or use memorised idioms unnaturally.

objectives.text: Describe people, places and experiences with precise adjectives and natural collocations (breathtaking view, highly recommend).
Use flexible phrases to give opinions, buy thinking time and paraphrase when a word is missing.
Use a small number of common idiomatic expressions accurately and only where they fit.

levels.foundation: Use four describing words and two thinking-time phrases in the long turn.
levels.core: Speak for the full two minutes using at least six word-bank items naturally.
levels.extension: Paraphrase one word you do not know instead of stopping ('the thing you use to ...').
levels.high_band: Use one idiomatic expression accurately and one precise collocation per point on the cue card, with no memorised sentences.

word_bank.example: The view from the top was breathtaking.
It is a bustling market, especially on Saturdays.
I'd highly recommend the local café.

word_bank.item: It's not something I've thought about much, but ...
word_bank.example: It's not something I've thought about much, but I suppose ...
As far as I'm concerned, public transport should be free.
I'd say it's mainly a question of money.
It depends on the age of the child.

word_bank.item: What I mean is ... / In other words ...
word_bank.example: In other words, it saves time.

word_bank.item: the thing you use to ... / a kind of ...
word_bank.example: a kind of small boat used for fishing

word_bank.meaning: something very special that rarely happens
word_bank.example: Seeing the northern lights was a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
Volunteering there was a real eye-opener.

word_bank.meaning: I was very surprised by what I saw
word_bank.example: When I saw the result, I couldn't believe my eyes.
Looking back, it was the best decision I made.

stages.title: Opening challenge: natural or memorised?
stages.student: Decide which answer sounds most natural.
stages.teacher: Read the three answers aloud. Learners vote; reveal comments.
stages.say: Examiners reward words used naturally, not idioms dropped in.
stages.check: Learners explain why Learner C sounds memorised.

stages.title: Word bank: describe, opine, rephrase
stages.student: Say each item aloud with your own example about your town or family.
stages.teacher: Drill stress and linking (I'd-HIGH-ly re-com-MEND; as-far-as-I'm-con-CERNED).
stages.say: Learn it as a chunk you can say smoothly.
stages.check: Each learner says four items with their own example.

stages.title: Match the phrase to its job
stages.student: Match each phrase to what it does in a conversation.
stages.teacher: Five minutes; reveal and practise each in a mini-dialogue.
stages.say: Know why you use a phrase, not just the phrase.

stages.title: Choose the natural answer
stages.student: Choose the most natural spoken response.
stages.teacher: Focus on wrong collocations and idioms in the wrong situation.
stages.say: If you are not sure an idiom fits, use a precise ordinary word.

stages.title: Prepare a long turn
stages.student: One minute to make notes: choose three word-bank items for the cue card.
stages.check: Every learner has three word-bank items noted.

stages.title: Speak and listen
stages.student: Speak for two minutes; your partner ticks each word-bank item they hear used naturally.
stages.teacher: Pairs, then swap. Listen live and note one precise word and one repeated word per learner.
stages.say: Keep going; rephrase if you lose a word.
stages.check: Each learner speaks for close to two minutes.

stages.title: Compare with the model
stages.student: Listen to or read the model; note two phrases to steal.
stages.teacher: Read the model aloud; ask which phrases were natural rather than impressive.
stages.say: The model is illustrative, not a target band.
stages.check: Each learner names two phrases to reuse.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket and note the homework.
stages.say: Record yourself once this week and count your repeated words.
stages.check: Every learner writes two new phrases.

blocks.title: Natural or memorised?
blocks.mode: Opening challenge; learners decide before the reveal
blocks.instructions: Examiner: 'Do you like the area where you live?' Three learners answered. Which answer is most natural?

examples.label: Learner A
examples.text: Yes, it's nice. It's very nice and very good. I like it very much.

examples.label: Learner B
examples.text: Yes, on the whole. It's quite a lively neighbourhood with a bustling market, although it can get noisy at weekends.
examples.comment: Best: precise collocations, a balanced view and natural softening ('on the whole', 'quite').

examples.label: Learner C
examples.text: Yes, it's raining cats and dogs of happiness there and every cloud has a silver lining.
examples.comment: Memorised idioms used wrongly. They do not fit the question and confuse the listener.

blocks.title: Match the phrase to its job
blocks.instructions: Match each phrase (1–8) to what it does, A–F. You may use a letter more than once.

items.prompt: It depends on how old you are.
As far as I'm concerned, it's too expensive.
items.evidence: As far as I'm concerned = my opinion

items.prompt: It's a kind of tool you use to open tins.
items.evidence: a kind of tool you use to = paraphrase
items.reason: Describes a word the speaker does not know.

items.prompt: Looking back, I should have studied harder.
That's an interesting question. Let me think ...
What I mean is, it saves people a lot of time.
I'd say most people prefer the city.
It's not something I've thought about much, but ...

blocks.title: Choose the natural answer
blocks.instructions: Choose the most natural spoken answer, A, B or C.

items.prompt: Describe the view from a place you visited.
items.reason: A wrong collocation; C too vague.
options: A  The view was very breathtaken.
B  The view from the top was absolutely breathtaking.
C  The view was nice and good.

items.prompt: Would you recommend the restaurant?
items.reason: B wrong collocation ('strongly' is less natural); C wrong grammar.
options: A  Definitely, I'd highly recommend it, especially the fish.
B  Yes, I very recommend it.
C  Yes, I recommend to go there it.

items.prompt: Tell me about a memorable trip.
items.evidence: once-in-a-lifetime experience fits a special trip
items.reason: A idiom in the wrong context; B unnatural.
options: A  It was a piece of cake trip and I broke the ice.
B  The trip was very memorable and memorable.
C  Climbing the volcano was a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

items.prompt: Describe your best friend's personality.
options: A  She's really easy-going; nothing seems to stress her.
C  She is the apple of my eye of friends.

items.prompt: You forget the word 'ladder'.
items.reason: A stops; C uses the wrong word.
options: A  I used ... sorry, I don't know the word.
B  I used one of those things you climb up to reach high places.

items.prompt: Do you think children should have phones?
options: B  Every child in the world must have a phone at once.
C  It depends on their age. For younger children, I'd say it's probably unnecessary.

blocks.title: Part 2 long turn with the word bank
blocks.mode: Pair practice; live feedback from partner and teacher
blocks.instructions: You will have one minute to prepare and up to two minutes to speak. Use at least six word-bank items naturally.
prompts: Describe a place you have visited that you would like to visit again. You should say: where it is; when you went there; what you did there; and explain why you would like to go back.
blocks.routine: 1 minute notes (keywords only) → 2 minutes speaking → partner ticks word-bank items heard → swap.
blocks.observation: Teacher and partner judge vocabulary from what is heard live; pronunciation comments are limited to what was heard live in class.

models.label: Illustrative long turn (not a certified band answer)
models.text: The place I'd like to go back to is a small lakeside town in the mountains, about three hours from where I live. I went there two summers ago with my cousins. It's not something I'd normally choose, because I'm more of a city person, but looking back, it was a real eye-opener. The town itself is fairly quiet, but there's a bustling market every Sunday where local farmers sell honey and cheese. We hired a kind of small rowing boat – I think it's called a canoe – and paddled to the far side of the lake, and honestly, the view of the mountains reflected in the water was breathtaking. The people were very down-to-earth, too; one family even invited us for tea. As for why I'd like to go back, I'd say it's mainly because I felt completely relaxed there, which is rare for me. I'd highly recommend it to anyone who needs a break from city life.

blocks.title: Homework: make it natural
blocks.mode: Homework; checked at the start of the next lesson
blocks.instructions: Complete each spoken answer with ONE word.

items.prompt: The market is really ______ on Saturdays – it's full of people.
As ______ as I'm concerned, homework should be shorter.
I'd ______ recommend this book to teenagers.
My grandfather is very down-to-______.
Visiting the hospital as a volunteer was a real eye-______.
Looking ______, I'm glad I chose to study abroad.

exit_ticket: Two describing words I will use instead of 'nice':
My favourite phrase for buying thinking time:
One idiom I can use correctly, with an example:
homework: Complete the natural-answer sentences on the homework sheet.
Record a one-minute answer to 'Describe a person who has influenced you'. Listen back and replace two repeated words.
delayed_followup: In Lesson 16 or 20 (Speaking Part 3 and full interview), note whether learners use precise collocations and recovery phrases instead of stopping. Record it as a later observation.
mapping_notes: Focuses use Diagnostic Bible section 7.2 construct names where they apply (lexical resource, paraphrase recognition). Teaching focuses only. This optional vocabulary lesson sits outside the 24-lesson sequence and changes no scoring, screener, readiness or band logic.

followup.status: WITHHELD from students until the planned fresh check; approved with lesson v1.0.0 on 2026-10-26. Keep private until use.
followup.delivery: About one teaching week later: 8 minutes, no word bank. Record timing and support.
followup.review: Score each answer independently; accept only natural, accurate phrases. Do not convert to an IELTS band.
followup.difficulty_calibration: Editorial relative-difficulty labels only. They do not imply an IELTS band, psychometric calibration, or verified difficulty.

blocks.title: Fresh check: choose the natural reply
blocks.instructions: Questions 1-4: choose the most natural reply, A, B or C. Questions 5-6: complete each reply with ONE word.

items.prompt: What is your home town famous for?
options: A  It is famous for good things and nice things.
B  It is famous for its very breathtaken nature.
C  It's best known for its hot springs, which attract quite a lot of visitors in winter.

items.prompt: Is it better to live alone or with family?
options: A  I suppose it depends on your stage of life. Students often benefit from living with family because it's cheaper.
C  Home is where the heart is and the early bird catches the worm.

items.prompt: Describe a day when you were very surprised.
options: A  I was surprised very much like a surprise.
B  When I opened the envelope and saw I'd won, I couldn't believe my eyes.
C  It was raining cats and dogs of surprise.

items.prompt: You forget the word 'thermometer'.
options: C  I used the thing you use to measure how hot something is.

items.prompt: In other ______, the new park has made the area much greener.
Watching the sunrise from the mountain was a once-in-a-______ experience.
